Subject: Planning our SDK cutover (v1 -> v2)

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're ready to move our app integration from your public v1 endpoint to the v2 SDK-based flow. A few constraints from our side:
- We need a staged traffic migration (canary) with the ability to stop/rollback immediately.
- Target p99 generation latency should stay under ~300ms for short prompts; longer prompts OK to vary.
- Our traffic is ~500 qps peak; we expect bursts but want rate-limit guidance.
- We require idempotency for our retry logic and prefer guidance on timeouts/backoff.

Can you share a concrete cutover checklist we can run in our staging window, a short snippet to initialize the SDK with timeouts/retries, and the suggested traffic-shift percentages and time windows?

Also we have a SOC2 evidence request coming in May — anything we should flag on your side for the migration?

Thanks,
Katie

Katie —

Appreciate the clear constraints. I've sketched a pragmatic "lift & guard" plan below (attached full cutover-runbook and traffic-shift-plan.xlsx). High-level:

1) Prep (staging, smoke tests) — 48–72 hrs before cutover
   - Deploy SDK v2 to staging; run synthetic p99/throughput test against staging endpoint
   - Verify KV-cache behavior with representative traffic
   - Confirm observability hooks (trace IDs, per-request cost tokens) are present

2) Canary (10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%)
   - Windows: 20m per step for first two steps, 45m for 50%, then 60m at 100%
   - Rollback trigger: 3 consecutive 5m windows with error rate >1.5% or p99 latency >450ms

3) Guard rails & operational actions
   - Circuit breaker on client (recommended threshold: 5xx rate >0.8% over 5m)
   - Backoff policy and idempotency keys (see Monica's snippet)
   - Rate-limit handling: honor 429 + Retry-After, and surface server-side rate metadata (we add x-rw-rl and x-rw-rl-reset headers)

4) Post-cutover verification (24–72h)
   - Traffic reconciliation, token usage, and correctness checks; run dedicated prompt set for quality regressions

I've attached: sdk-setup-steps.pdf (quick checklist), traffic-shift-plan.xlsx (timetable + who/when), cutover-runbook.md (play-by-play).

Proposed call to walk the runbook Thursday 4/12 10am PT — does that work for your team?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference

Hi Katie —

Adding a compact SDK init + retry/backoff example you can drop directly into your gateway. The key points we aim for:
- Short client-side connect timeout (200ms) and per-call server timeout (1200ms) for generation calls
- Exponential backoff with jitter and an upper cap; honor 429 Retry-After header when present
- Use idempotency keys for non-idempotent requests (create/update flows)

Javascript (Node) sample (extract):

const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference-sdk');
const client = new Redwood.Client({
  apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY,
  baseUrl: 'https://api.redwood.com/v2',
  connectTimeoutMs: 200,
  requestTimeoutMs: 1200,
});

async function safeGenerate(prompt, options = {}) {
  const idempotencyKey = options.idempotencyKey || generateUUID();
  const maxAttempts = 4;
  let attempt = 0;
  while (attempt < maxAttempts) {
    try {
      return await client.generate({ prompt, idempotencyKey, timeoutMs: 1000 });
    } catch (err) {
      attempt++;
      const retryAfter = parseInt(err.headers && err.headers['retry-after'], 10);
      if (err.statusCode === 429 && retryAfter) {
        await wait(retryAfter * 1000 + jitter());
      } else if (shouldRetry(err) && attempt < maxAttempts) {
        await wait(Math.min(1000 * Math.pow(2, attempt) + jitter(), 5000));
      } else {
        throw err;
      }
    }
  }
}

Python sample (requests + simple backoff) is attached as sample-retries.js (text file with both examples).

A few server-side headers to watch for in responses: x-rw-rl (remaining), x-rw-rl-reset (seconds to reset), x-rw-trace (trace id). If you see steady x-rw-rl <= 50 on a client pool, consider smoothing client concurrency.

I'll attach the sample file (sample-retries.js) and also include a short checklist for SDK environment variables.

—Monica

Subject: Re: Planning our SDK cutover (v1 -> v2) — rollout & monitoring

Katie / Team —

Thanks all. A few operational guardrails we enforce during cutovers at Redwood:
- Observability: create a temporary dashboard scope for the cutover (p50/p95/p99, 5xx%, 429%, RU consumption) and add your SRE on-view
- Rollforward cadence: we do 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with health checks as Karthik outlined. Extend the 25% window if you see p99 variance during the second step.
- Circuit breaker: we recommend an outboard circuit that trips when error >0.8% for 5m AND p99 > 450ms. Immediate rollback if tripped.

Attached is a short runbook section for quick rollback commands and a sample Terraform snippet showing how to configure the SDK client host and fallback endpoints for graceful degradation. Also included: a minimal exponential backoff helper you can port into any gateway.

Exponential backoff (pseudocode):
function waitWithJitter(baseMs, attempt, capMs = 5000) {
  const raw = Math.min(capMs, baseMs * Math.pow(2, attempt));
  return raw / 2 + Math.random() * (raw / 2); // full jitter\}

Monitoring thresholds (suggested):
- Error rate (5xx + 4xx unexpected): alert at 0.5% (pager), escalation at 1.5%
- p99: page at >450ms for 10 minutes continuous
- RU consumption: alert at 85% quota of expected commit

I'll attend the 4/12 call; if you want we can add a short postmortem step to the runbook template to capture any regressions.

—Vivek
